question_en: Which game and which area is the scene in the image from?
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-2-2-A02

## Step 01 · Extract Combined Clues from the Rainy Stone Pillar Scene

**Action:** Record identifiable objects and locations from the input image. Possible search queries include examples like "pixel game rain water pillar reflection" or "Yume Nikki-style game rain stone pillars reflection" to find matching images in community scene galleries.

**Evidence Observation:** The image is a top-down pixel art scene. On the left, there is a thick stone pillar with vertical grooves and a multi-layered base; the top of the pillar extends beyond the frame. A reflection is visible below the base. A small character is located near the center. Pointed rocks are present on the right and in the distance. Thin diagonal rain lines are scattered across the dark water surface. The scene supports this combination of objects; relying solely on the character's art style or the generic "dark and rainy" atmosphere is insufficient to determine the specific game and area.

**Step Result:** Use the combined layout of the stone pillar, reflection, rocks, and rain lines as the basis for subsequent matching.

## Step 02 · Verify the Original Rainy Image Within Named Screenshot Groups

**Action:** Review the public mirror extraction of the `daily-ynfg-worlds` screenshot posts saved in the question package. Check the group of four images under the entry titled "Stagnant Bottom" and open its original rainy CDN image.

**Evidence Observation:** The mirror save text lists "Stagnant Bottom," with tags including `yume 2kki`. This entry includes four images. The saved `rainy.jpg` corresponds to the input: the pillar body and base on the left, the reflection below, the character's position relative to the base, the distribution of rocks on the right, and the rain lines all match. The suffix of the original image URL is `.pnj`, while the saved file is actually a JPEG; this is merely a detail regarding the source format and does not affect the scene correspondence.

Public mirror entry for the Stagnant Bottom screenshot post:
https://www.tumgik.com/tag/fog%20ynfg

Actual CDN original image of the rainy scene:
https://64.media.tumblr.com/f72edc489a7fde945771140ce5fc314a/9339984a2d61d5a7-ee/s400x600/15074cf5ffca681c739f4337c9ea1a0766bd50e3.pnj

**Step Result:** Obtained matching clues for Yume 2kki / Stagnant Bottom. The permanent link to the original Tumblr post was not recovered in the question package, so one cannot claim to have accessed it; the input and the original rainy image are also screenshots from the same source. The next step is to verify the name using area data.

## Step 03 · Verify Area Name and Different States of the Same Area

**Action:** Read the saved search extraction of the English area entry and the saved webpage extraction of the Japanese entry. Compare them with the foggy image from the same group to check whether a weather state or an indoor scene was mistakenly written as the area name.

**Evidence Observation:** The English entry is titled "Yume 2kki: Stagnant Bottom," with "Regional Name(s)" listing 霧色の湖 (Kiriiro no Mizuumi). The main text explains that this area has shallow water, huge stone pillars, and rocks, and can change from foggy to rainy. The Japanese entry for 霧色の湖 also directly lists the English name "Stagnant Bottom" and mentions the pillars and that the fog clears and rain starts after touching plants. In the foggy reference, the gray fog is obvious and the character is between two pillars, which differs from the input's clear rain lines and the framing of a single pillar on the left; however, it is another state of the same area, not a different area. The two room images in this group feature an indoor composition with tables, chairs, lamps, and windows, and cannot replace the input's outdoor water surface scene.

Yume Wiki: Stagnant Bottom area entry:
https://yume.wiki/2kki/Stagnant_Bottom

Japanese area entry: 霧色の湖:
https://wikiwiki.jp/yume2kki-t/%E9%9C%A7%E8%89%B2%E3%81%AE%E6%B9%96

Original reference image of the foggy state in the same area:
https://64.media.tumblr.com/f8052c1a567ee786915d904df7ce1bb3/9339984a2d61d5a7-38/s400x600/c99b066f51c2ccd4eb6dfd84d3c68977eec6e79d.pnj

Original reference image of the dark room in the same group:
https://64.media.tumblr.com/5b0e2702d9fe762d15a50534e050bbc3/9339984a2d61d5a7-4c/s400x600/50f9a07af7b2278f668c1d52308e7c45e90b3d0e.pnj

Original reference image of the bright room in the same group:
https://64.media.tumblr.com/c45e228a2ac66aa30a343680ec3a8589/9339984a2d61d5a7-d9/s400x600/8724e6212146d87e8752f090e402e4f98877bcf7.pnj

**Step Result:** The screenshot attribution and bilingual area naming are consistent; the answer only needs to retain the game and area. The direct link to the English page previously timed out; the current basis is the saved search extraction, so one cannot write that all pages were successfully crawled. The static question image has no sound, so there is no need to divert to music tracks or areas with the same song for further retrieval.

## Final Answer

Yume 2kki；Stagnant Bottom
